solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police dog out quietly playing with President

indicators.note: playing suggests the remaining letters are played about with and rearranged
out says a letter is dropped from the police dog phrase before it is rearranged

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A police dog is let out to play quietly beside the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes P (quietly) from POLICE DOG, and 'playing' rearranges the remaining OLICEDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Coolidge was the thirtieth President of the United States.

clue.text: Roman emperor is up and about to depart for part of America

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed name encloses the next piece
in a down clue, being up means the emperor's name is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Nero is the classic Roman emperor of crosswords
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: An emperor rises and is about to leave for part of America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is up' means read upwards; 'about' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state in the north-west of the USA, so one part of America.

clue.text: Foreigners lack initial rights

indicators.note: lack initial says the first letter of the word for foreigners is missing

parts.note: aliens are foreigners

explanation.surface: Foreigners do not have basic rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack initial' takes the A from the front of ALIENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Decide to settle

definitions.meaning: to decide something is to fix or resolve it
to settle a matter is to fix it conclusively

explanation.definitionFit: Both definitions mean to fix or resolve a question firmly, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: In a group, coming from France

definitions.text: In a group, coming from France

parts.words: In a group, coming from France
parts.note: a French phrase meaning all together, borrowed into English

explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from France' tells the solver the phrase for 'in a group' is a French one used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression means all together, as a body or crowd.

clue.text: Guard dog — watch out!

indicators.note: out here means the watch word lies outside, round the dog

parts.note: to see is to watch
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A warning to look out for a guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard dog' reads as one thing, but the definition is 'Guard' alone; 'out' signals the watch word goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard something is to make it safe, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Involved with swindle, right to get out hurriedly

indicators.note: involved with means wrapped up in, so the right letter sits inside the swindle

parts.note: a scam is a swindle

explanation.surface: Someone mixed up in a fraud does the right thing and flees.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command or verb meaning to leave in a hurry.

clue.text: In 13 across, on 16 across Day, take car, beetle off — enjoy!

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so the car and beetle letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Americans on Independence Day should take the car, drive the Beetle out, and have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CARBEETLE. 13 across is the UNITED STATES and 16 across INDEPENDENCE, setting the Fourth of July scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate is to mark an occasion with festivity and enjoyment, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Found the solution again, having made up one's mind

definitions.meaning: worked out a problem once more, taking the prefix re- with solved
determined, having come to a decision

explanation.definitionFit: The word splits as re-solved, solved again, and also means determined or decided.

clue.text: He takes charge temporarily, for example, during gap

indicators.note: during means within, so the example sits inside the gap

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gap

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for a while, for instance in an interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who is a child or absent, so temporarily.

clue.text: Preacher has spoken in some obscurity

indicators.note: in places the word for spoken inside the obscurity

parts.note: mist is a kind of obscurity, something that hides the view
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A preacher's words are somewhat unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link here; 'in' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist lectures others on right conduct, as a preacher does.

clue.text: Associates with swindling types?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., kinds of people who con others

explanation.definitionFit: To consort with is to keep company with, and the word splits as con plus sorts, swindling types.

clue.text: Having one's own transport somewhere in Alabama?

definitions.meaning: able to get about, with a car
a port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a car is mobile, and Mobile is a city in Alabama.

clue.text: A1 student set out for the country

indicators.note: out signals the letters are set in a new order, as in worked out

parts.note: the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A top-class student departs for the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AI (A1 with the 1 as I), STUDENT and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a country, the USA.

clue.text: American Lesley's going out with, to no avail

indicators.note: going out suggests changing shape, so the letters of Lesley's are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American dates Lesley, but nothing comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like dating, but it is the anagram signal; the apostrophe's S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something uselessly is doing it to no avail, without result.

clue.text: Senator is involved with foreign girls

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled up, so the letters of senator and is are scrambled

explanation.surface: A senator has affairs with girls from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Senoritas are young Spanish women, girls from a foreign country.

clue.text: Very good article for cake decoration

parts.note: angelic means extremely good, like an angel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A most excellent item for decorating a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied angelica stems are used to decorate cakes.

clue.text: US city that was gained by America in 1783

definitions.meaning: a city in Missouri, near Kansas City

definitions.text: that was gained by America in 1783
definitions.meaning: freedom from British rule, confirmed by the Treaty of Paris

explanation.definitionFit: Independence is a city in Missouri, and the freedom America won when Britain recognised it in 1783.

clue.text: Two thousand and one in fees? They're not real

indicators.note: in places the numerals inside the word for fees

parts.note: dues are fees paid
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two thousand and one included in charges, as if a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a date, the year 2001; the numbers are Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummies are imitations or replicas, things that are not genuine.

clue.text: Not wholly employed on the stage

definitions.meaning: acting a role, being in a part in a play

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly, and an actor with a role is literally in a part.

clue.text: Turnover in coats

parts.note: the turned-back edge of a coat front showing its lining, a lapel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' reads like a business figure or a pastry, but it is literal: a part of the coat turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Revers are the turned-back edges of a garment, like lapels on a coat.

clue.text: Show disdain for bad puns about royalty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the royal letter
bad means faulty, so the letters of puns are messed up

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen, so royalty

explanation.surface: Royals look down on poor wordplay about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges PUNS into SPUN, and 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt, showing disdain.

clue.text: Queen to disembark in state

parts.note: Mary is the name of several English queens
to land is to come ashore from a ship

explanation.surface: A queen steps off a ship in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maryland is one of the states of the USA, a crossword-standard example.

clue.text: See purpose of parasite

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a use is a purpose

explanation.surface: Look at what a parasite is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small insect that lives on its host, a parasite.

clue.text: Girl nymph loses her head in part of 13 across

parts.note: a miss is a girl

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter goes from the nymph word

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful nymph of the Islamic paradise

explanation.surface: A girl, a sort of nymph, gets beheaded somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses her head' takes H from HOURI, leaving OURI.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the states of the USA, 13 across being the United States.

clue.text: President may appear as odd in brown

indicators.note: in places the word for odd inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
rum is a British informal word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: The President looks peculiar in a brown suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym; 'in' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S Truman was the thirty-third President of the United States.

clue.text: May be grand study about some in deep depression

indicators.note: about means round, so the study word goes round the word for some

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: A great study of some in a very low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be grand' points to the Grand Canyon in Arizona; 'deep depression' sounds like low spirits but is a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, a depression in the land.

clue.text: Around America, parking in schools raises doubts

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations inside the word for schools

parts.note: schools of thought are sects

explanation.surface: Across America, parking near schools makes people suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' and 'in' together describe the enclosure, the schools word wrapping round the abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to doubt it, a verb synonym.
